title: Unknown human physiology in partial gravity
bottleneck: Microgravity devastates the body — bone loss, muscle atrophy, vision changes, immune shifts — and Earth's 1 g is fine, but nobody knows where the threshold lies between them. The Moon's 1/6 g and Mars' 3/8 g have never hosted long-term human stays, and animal centrifuge data does not cleanly extrapolate. Countermeasures designed for zero-g may be overkill or insufficient at partial g, and we will not know until crews live there for months.
why_it_blocks: If 3/8 g still causes serious deconditioning, Mars surface missions need artificial gravity or aggressive countermeasures that reshape habitat design; if it is sufficient, architectures simplify enormously. The uncertainty forces designing for the worst case.
current_state: No human has spent more than about 3 days in partial gravity (Apollo). ISS research covers only 0 g; proposed variable-gravity research stations remain unfunded concepts.
